title: Refresh the automatic USB product after changing MCU architecture
problem: Kconfig saves the evaluated MCU name as USB_PRODUCT. On the next menuconfig run it treats that value as an explicit selection, so switching from STM32F446 to RP2040 leaves the USB descriptor and /dev/serial/by-id path labelled stm32f446xx.
reproduce: Create a saved STM32F446 USB configuration, reload it, then select RP2040 USB. The pinned baseline reports MCU=rp2040 while USB_PRODUCT remains stm32f446xx.
acceptance: When the prior USB product matched the prior MCU and the user changes architecture without editing the product, the saved product follows the new MCU. Existing custom products, a product edited during the switch, and abandoned unsaved menu changes remain unchanged.
repair: Route make menuconfig through a small project wrapper. It records the saved MCU/product identity before opening the vendored UI, reloads only the configuration actually saved by that UI, and clears the stale user value when it still represents the old automatic default.

verification.limitations: BCL reproduces and repairs the complete saved Kconfig transition without flashing firmware. It does not enumerate the resulting USB descriptor on physical STM32 or RP2040 hardware.
verification.ownerCheck: Reuse an STM32F446 USB .config, run make menuconfig, switch to RP2040 USB, save and build. Confirm CONFIG_USB_PRODUCT is rp2040 and the flashed device appears under a usb-Klipper_rp2040_* path. Repeat once with an explicit custom USB product and confirm it remains custom.

publish.commitMessage: kconfig: Refresh automatic USB product on MCU switch
